extracted.intended_audience: Cornell faculty and researchers (Ithaca campus and Weill Cornell Medicine) preparing grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit evaluation criteria for preparing externally funded research proposals at Cornell (both Ithaca and Weill Cornell Medicine), including funder-specific emphases, pre-award administrative expectations, and Cornell-specific framing. Useful for drafting Specific Aims, budgets, compliance plans, and collaborative proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Specific Aims with clear hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong Specific Aims with clear hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cornell emphasizes hypothesis-driven aims; aims should be concise, hypothesis-focused, and convey the project’s central question. This appears in the OSP 'What Wins' list and is reinforced in Specific Aims conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent aims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be structured so each can succeed/fail independently (avoid serial dependency). Explicitly called out under Cornell-specific Specific Aims conventions and in the 'What Wins' list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative preliminary results where possible to demonstrate feasibility and support claims. Listed in 'What Wins' and repeated in implicit rubric themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit rigor language and statistical plan
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State rigor and reproducibility measures explicitly, including a clear statistical analysis plan. The page highlights 'rigor language explicit' and separately mentions 'statistical analysis plan' as an implicit theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage Cornell-specific facilities and cores
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and plan to use Cornell resources (e.g., CNF, CHESS, Cornell Center for Materials Research, Statistical Consulting Unit, library, departmental cores). Use these to demonstrate institutional support and available infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine cross-campus or cross-disciplinary collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-campus or cross-disciplinary collaborations where genuine
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborations between Ithaca and Weill Cornell or across colleges are valued when authentic. The guidance cautions that collaborations should be genuine (not token) and highlights cross-campus centers (Atkinson, Cornell Tech) as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder and extension engagement for USDA NIFA projects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDA/AFRI proposals should include stakeholder engagement, producer partnerships, extension components (Cornell Cooperative Extension), and multi-state collaborations. These strengthen relevance and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry partnerships where relevant (Cornell Tech, engineering)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry partnerships are valued especially for Cornell Tech, engineering, and translational projects; document roles and benefits of industry collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budget including Cornell indirect rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Realistic budget with Cornell indirect rate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets should be realistic, use the correct Cornell indirect (F&A) rates, and reflect actual costs. OSP offers budget development and will catch budget errors pre-submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance issues proactively addressed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and resolve compliance requirements early (IRB, IACUC, export controls, human subjects protections). The page specifically flags Weill Cornell NYC IRB/NYC compliance gaps as common pre-submission issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims structure and drafting process (Cornell conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Four-Paragraph Structure; Hypothesis-driven aims; Conceptual figure encouraged; Iterate 10+ times
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cornell recommends a standard four-paragraph Specific Aims page: hypothesis-driven content, aim independence, include a conceptual figure if helpful, and iterate the Aims 10+ times through drafting and feedback (mock review/consultations available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award administrative completeness (budget, subawards, cost-sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget development; Subaward agreements; Cost-sharing analysis; Submission via Cornell eSubmit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSP provides pre-award services: develop accurate budgets, negotiate and document subawards (pay attention to Ithaca–NYC subaward issues), analyze cost-share requirements, and prepare for submission through Cornell eSubmit. These administrative elements must be correct prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward clarity and management
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define subaward scopes, budgets, and responsibilities; anticipate and resolve Ithaca–NYC subaward complications. OSP flags subaward complications during pre-submission review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and required sections compliance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow funder formatting rules and include all required sections. OSP commonly catches format violations and missing sections during pre-submission checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator–environment fit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that investigators’ expertise and the institutional environment/resources support successful project completion (e.g., connections to cores, clinical affiliations for NIH translational work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic timeline and scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should present feasible scope, timelines, and milestones aligned with available resources and personnel; unrealistic scope is a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align with Cornell’s land-grant/public mission when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Land-Grant Public Mission — 'Any person, any study'; public service orientation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable (especially USDA, Hatch/McIntire-Stennis), emphasize public-service impact, extension outcomes, producer partnerships, and practical/translational benefits consistent with Cornell’s land-grant heritage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational framing where applicable (Weill + Ithaca bridging)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For projects with translational potential (Weill Cornell clinical affiliates, veterinary–human medicine bridges), frame aims to show pathway to translation and clinical or applied impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF-specific expectations: Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address both Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts explicitly; partnerships with Cornell Cooperative Extension, 4-H, and K–12 outreach strengthen Broader Impacts claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH-specific expectations and local strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH — standard NIH conventions; translational framing; NYC cohort access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH application conventions (formatting, biosketches, etc.), emphasize translational framing when relevant, and highlight access to NYC patient cohorts and clinical partnerships (NewYork-Presbyterian, MSK, HSS) for Weill Cornell proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: USDA NIFA-specific expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: USDA NIFA — AFRI themes, Hatch/McIntire-Stennis context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDA proposals should emphasize stakeholder engagement, producer partnerships, extension components (Cornell Cooperative Extension), multi-state collaborations, and practical outcomes; Hatch/McIntire-Stennis have formula fund reporting expectations.
